Креатин.about: Most Researched Sports Supplement: Helps muscles recapture ATP, the currency of short, powerful efforts.
Креатин.caution: The ONLY proven form is CREATINE MONOHYDRATE. HCl/ester/buffer - marketing. Long-term safe in healthy people (ISSN). The myth about the kidneys has been debunked. Water retention of 0.5-2 kg in the first weeks is normal.
Креатин.food_sources: Red meat and fish: about 4-5 g per kilogram of raw product - difficult to get enough of.
Креатин.guidelines: ISSN position: effective and safe; EFSA health claims for sports are not required.
Креатин.how_to_choose: Monohydrate (Creapure sign); without “transport systems” and overpayments for exotic forms.

interactions.note: risk of dehydration, drink more water
load on the kidneys with long-term use

mechs: Phosphocreatine buffer: ATP resynthesis in neurons and muscles
Brain energy metabolism: replenishment of brain stores of creatine phosphate for neurons
Creatine phosphate reserve in high intensity sets: more working repetitions
Increase in lean mass and strength in conjunction with strength training
Креатин.myths: “It hits the kidneys in healthy people” - not confirmed at standard doses. “It doesn’t work without loading” - it works, it’s just slower.
Креатин.name: Creatine
Креатин.onset: 2-4 weeks of regular use (with a loading period of 5-7 days); does not give an instant “tide”.
Креатин.title: Creatine
Креатин.upper_limit: There is no formal UL; 3-5 g/day is safe for a long time; above 10 g/day - GI discomfort.
Креатин.who_needs: Strength and sprint athletes; vegetarians and vegans (there is less creatine in muscles without meat); elderly – against loss of muscle mass.
